case.player_role: ER physician, leading the trauma resuscitation room
case.patient: Tom, a healthy 28-year-old man, 180 cm and 85 kg, with no pulmonary or cardiac history
case.handover: Tom caught his left leg between a wall and a forklift. The ambulance crew found a crush injury to the left thigh. The handover is done, Tom lies on the EmergencyBed and the ambulance crew has left.
case.task_distribution: Agreed in advance: the Anesthesiologist and the AnesthesiaAssistant stand at the head for A and B, the Nurse stands at the torso for C and D.

checkpoints.name: Arrival
checkpoints.patient: Conscious and adequately alert, but pale. Still dressed.
checkpoints.tom: Conscious. Answers questions adequately and does what he is asked, such as opening his mouth and sticking out his tongue.

findings.mouth: Nothing in the mouth, the airway is clear
findings.chest, with the upper body exposed: Symmetrical chest expansion 12 times per minute, no retractions, no tracheal deviation, no abnormal skin discoloration
findings.lung auscultation: Vesicular breath sounds in all 4 lung fields

checkpoints.advances_when: The team moves on to assessing circulation (C)

checkpoints.name: Shock signs
checkpoints.patient: Pale and now sweaty, which he was not before. Still conscious.

findings.mouth: Nothing in the mouth, the airway is clear
findings.lung auscultation: Vesicular breath sounds in all 4 lung fields

team.Nurse: Nervous about the patient, and says so to the physician

checkpoints.advances_when: A 2nd IV line is placed and blood is drawn for a complete lab panel

checkpoints.name: Loss of consciousness

findings.lung auscultation after intubation: Vesicular breath sounds in all lung fields, the tube is placed correctly

checkpoints.advances_when: Tom is intubated, the tube is secured and he is connected to the Ventilator

checkpoints.name: Worsening shock
checkpoints.patient: Unconscious and intubated, on the Ventilator. Circulation has deteriorated.
checkpoints.tom: Unconscious and intubated. Does not respond.

findings.lung auscultation: Vesicular breath sounds in all lung fields, the tube is placed correctly
findings.pulse: 115 bpm, weakly palpable at the carotid artery
findings.left thigh (under the clothing): Red and very swollen, from internal bleeding in the left thigh

checkpoints.advances_when: The physician asks for the trauma surgeon

checkpoints.name: Surgeon in the room
checkpoints.patient: Unconscious and intubated, in hypovolemic shock from bleeding in the left thigh.
checkpoints.tom: Unconscious and intubated. Does not respond.

findings.left thigh: Red and very swollen, from internal bleeding in the left thigh

team.Surgeon: Wants to operate as quickly as possible, and wants an X-ray of the left leg before Tom goes to the OR

checkpoints.advances_when: Tom leaves the room for the OR
